text: Washington runs its own OSHA plan (DOSH, at Labor and Industries) and its excavation rule is chapter 296-155 WAC, Part N. It is stricter than federal OSHA in three ways a crew will feel. 1) Depth: every employee in an excavation must be protected from cave-ins by a protective system (sloping, benching, shoring or a shield) unless the excavation is entirely in stable rock, or it is less than 4 ft deep and a competent person has examined the ground and found no indication of a potential cave-in (WAC 296-155-657(1)(a)). Federal OSHA draws that line at 5 ft. 2) Written plan, since June 1, 2026: the employer must have a competent person complete a written trench excavation work plan for any trench an employee may enter where a protective system is required; employees are trained on the plan before they go in, and the plan is kept on the job site. No written plan is needed when the trench is 4 ft or less and no protective system is required, or when the trench is sloped at 1.5 horizontal to 1 vertical or flatter (WAC 296-155-655(13)). 3) Competent person on site: a competent person must remain on the job site any time trench excavation work is being performed (WAC 296-155-655(13)(a)), and inspects the excavation, the area around it and the protective system daily, before work starts, as needed during the shift and after every rainstorm (WAC 296-155-655(11)). The rest matches the federal numbers: a ladder, stairway or ramp in trenches 4 ft or more deep with no more than 25 ft of lateral travel; spoil and equipment at least 2 ft back from the edge; test the air before entering an excavation deeper than 4 ft where a hazardous atmosphere could exist; digging up to 2 ft below the bottom of a shield only when the shield is rated for the full depth and no soil is being lost from behind or below it; sloping or benching for an excavation deeper than 20 ft designed by a registered professional engineer. Plain-language summary; the WAC text, your competent person and your company program govern.
title: Washington trench rules (WAC 296-155 Part N): protective system at 4 ft, written trench work plan, competent person on site
topic: State OSHA plans: where trench and confined space rules differ from federal OSHA

text: Washington's sloping table is Table N-1 in WAC 296-155-66403 (Part N, Appendix B). Maximum allowable slopes, horizontal to vertical, for excavations less than 20 ft deep: stable rock vertical (90 degrees); Type A soil 3/4 to 1 (53 degrees); Type B soil 1 to 1 (45 degrees); Type C soil 1 1/2 to 1 (34 degrees). Sloping or benching for an excavation deeper than 20 ft must be designed by a registered professional engineer. Where it differs from the federal table: the federal table (29 CFR 1926 Subpart P, Appendix B, Table B-1) has a note allowing a steeper short-term slope of 1/2 to 1 in Type A soil for excavations 12 ft or less that are open 24 hours or less. Table N-1 has no such note and the Washington appendix has no short-term allowance, so on a Washington job Type A is 3/4 to 1 no matter how short a time the trench is open. The Type A, B and C angles themselves are the same as federal. When the slope shows signs of distress, cut it back at least 1/2 horizontal to 1 vertical flatter than the maximum allowable slope. The app's Trench Sloping screen uses the same 3/4, 1 and 1 1/2 to 1 values and does not use the short-term slope, so its result fits Washington; remember that Washington requires protection from 4 ft, not 5 ft. The competent person classifies the soil and picks the slope; this is a plain-language summary and the WAC text governs.
title: Washington trench sloping (WAC 296-155-66403, Table N-1): maximum slopes by soil type, no steeper short-term slope in Type A
